name: mkfs
description: Creates (formats) a filesystem on a partition or disk — mkfs.ext4, mkfs.xfs, mkfs.vfat are its concrete forms.

flags.description: Filesystem type: ext4, xfs, btrfs, vfat, f2fs.
The explicit form most people actually use.
ext4: show what would be created, write nothing.

examples.output:
Creating filesystem with 244188672 4k blocks
Creating journal (32768 blocks): done
examples.explanation: Formats the partition as ext4. ALL previous data on it is gone.
Creates an XFS filesystem with the label "data" — XFS is the RHEL default and excels at large files and parallel I/O.
FAT32 — the type USB sticks need to be readable by cameras, cars, and Windows.

about: Choosing a filesystem: ext4 is the safe universal default; XFS scales better for huge files and is RHEL's default; Btrfs adds snapshots and checksumming (openSUSE default); FAT32/exFAT are for cross-device compatibility. mkfs only creates the filesystem — partition first with fdisk/parted.
mistakes: Running mkfs on the whole disk (/dev/sdb) instead of a partition (/dev/sdb1) — legal but usually not what you want.
Formatting the wrong disk — there is no undo.
warnings: mkfs DESTROYS all data on the target without asking. Verify the device with lsblk before every run.
